files.purpose: Configure Jac 0.36.1 [project] with name agewise_backend, kind service and entry-point main.jac; this headless slice has no npm dependencies and no extra dependency tables (byllm ships with jaclang).

Define node Patient, the hub of the graph, with required name:str and str fields defaulting to "": dob, medicare_id, medicaid_id, address, city, state, zip_code, phone, email, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, created_at, updated_at, plus primary_language:str default "English". No abilities.

signatures.Patient: node Patient { has name: str, dob: str = "", medicare_id: str = "", medicaid_id: str = "", address: str = "", city: str = "", state: str = "", zip_code: str = "", phone: str = "", email: str = "", emergency_contact_name: str = "", emergency_contact_phone: str = "", primary_language: str = "English", created_at: str = "", updated_at: str = ""; }

files.purpose: Define node Document for a raw incoming document. Every field has a default so Document(...) can be built with keywords only: doc_id, doc_type, title, raw_content, raw_text, source, original_filename, mime_type, ingested_at, plain_english_summary, embedding_id, content_hash are str default ""; source_channel:str default "email"; classification:str default "UNKNOWN" (the sentinel for not yet classified); processed:bool default False. No abilities.

signatures.Document: node Document { has doc_id: str = "", doc_type: str = "", title: str = "", raw_content: str = "", raw_text: str = "", source: str = "", source_channel: str = "email", classification: str = "UNKNOWN", original_filename: str = "", mime_type: str = "", ingested_at: str = "", processed: bool = False, plain_english_summary: str = "", embedding_id: str = "", content_hash: str = ""; }

files.purpose: Import environ from os and Model from jaclang.byllm.lib. Declare glob llm = Model(model_name="openrouter/anthropic/claude-4.6-sonnet", api_key=environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")). Declare two body-less LLM functions delegated with by llm(model=llm) and described by sem strings: classify_document returns ONLY one category name from EOB, MSN_PART_A, MSN_PART_B, MEDICAL_BILL, CMS1500_CLAIM, UB04_CLAIM, INSURANCE_NOTICE, POLICY_CHANGE, HIPAA_AUTH, POWER_OF_ATTORNEY, WILL, TRUST, BENEFICIARY_FORM, LEGAL_NOTICE, FINANCIAL_STATEMENT, APPOINTMENT_CONFIRMATION, PRESCRIPTION_NOTICE, SCAM_COMMUNICATION, UNKNOWN; translate_to_plain_english rewrites technical medical billing or legal content at about a 6th-grade reading level for a 75-year-old reader, ending with a one-sentence 'Bottom line:' summary. The module-level name must be exactly llm so tests can replace it with MockLLM; the returned string is used as-is by callers.

signatures.classify_document: def classify_document(raw_text: str, source_metadata: dict) -> str by llm(model=llm);
signatures.translate_to_plain_english: def translate_to_plain_english(technical_content: str, content_type: str, reading_level: int = 6) -> str by llm(model=llm);

files.purpose: Import Patient from graph.nodes.patient, Document from graph.nodes.document and classify_document from abilities.llm_abilities (absolute imports). walker DocumentClassify has no fields. On Patient entry it visits all outgoing neighbours ([-->]), in connection order. On Document entry: if here.classification != "UNKNOWN" it executes disengage, which ends the ENTIRE walk (later documents are not visited and no model call is made). Otherwise it builds source_meta = {"source": here.source, "filename": here.original_filename, "mime_type": here.mime_type}, calls classify_document(raw_text=here.raw_content, source_metadata=source_meta), assigns the returned string unchanged to here.classification, and prints "[DocumentClassify] Document <doc_id> classified as: <category>". It reports nothing.

signatures.DocumentClassify: walker DocumentClassify { can start with Patient entry; can classify with Document entry; }

files.purpose: Import Patient from graph.nodes.patient, Document from graph.nodes.document and translate_to_plain_english from abilities.llm_abilities (absolute imports). walker PlainEnglishTranslator has no fields. On Patient entry it visits [-->] in connection order. On Document entry: if here.plain_english_summary != "" or here.raw_content == "" it executes disengage, ending the ENTIRE walk (later documents keep their summary unchanged and no model call is made). Otherwise it calls translate_to_plain_english(technical_content=here.raw_content[:4000], content_type=here.classification, reading_level=6), stores the returned string unchanged in here.plain_english_summary (classification is not modified), and prints "[PlainEnglishTranslator] Translated doc <doc_id> (<classification>)". It reports nothing.

signatures.PlainEnglishTranslator: walker PlainEnglishTranslator { can start with Patient entry; can translate with Document entry; }

files.purpose: Thin entry module holding only imports: Patient, Document, classify_document, translate_to_plain_english, DocumentClassify and PlainEnglishTranslator from their modules (graph.nodes.patient, graph.nodes.document, abilities.llm_abilities, graph.walkers.intake.document_classify, graph.walkers.intake.plain_english_translator). No other code.

verify.flow: Patient ++> Document -> spawn DocumentClassify -> spawn PlainEnglishTranslator -> read node fields
verify.steps: Run jac check main.jac. In tests, import abilities.llm_abilities as a module and assign its llm to MockLLM(model_name="mockllm", config={"outputs": [...]}) from jaclang.byllm.lib before spawning; outputs are consumed one per by-llm call in order across both walkers. Assert classification/plain_english_summary values and the disengage-stops-walk behavior.
